findings.summary: The rule list is hand-picked, and the pin test only checks rules the brief already quotes. It does not cover the class.
findings.evidence: VERDICT_RULES in verify.rs has three rows: D43, D63 ('as one whole simple command inside a chained or piped one') and D115. The plan quotes D43 and D115 and leaves out D63, although its own decision 5 depends on that rule ('The verifier runs only whole simple commands'). The pin test iterates over the plan's own (constant, source) table. If a fourth row is added to VERDICT_RULES, or D63 changes, no test fails and the brief silently omits the rule. The plan says the test 'covers the class (any criterion-judging rule the brief quotes)', but that only holds for rules the brief already chose to quote. The reading promised a section 'built from live facts'. Fix: Drive the verdict-rule part of the test from the enforcing table, not a hand list. In the athena-context test, take the VERDICT_RULES block from include_str!(verify.rs), extract every `id:` and `source:` pair, and assert each id has a line in the 'Rules that judge criteria' section that quotes its source. Then a new or reworded verdict rule fails the test. Add a D63 line, the whole-simple-command rule, to the section. Do the same for DEFAULT_WRITTEN_FILES in checks.rs: assert every path it lists is named in the section. This stays within scope, because verify.rs and checks.rs are only read.
findings.location: Plan Decisions 3 and Step 4; Demonstration for criterion 2; crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs:1197-1238 (VERDICT_RULES)

findings.summary: The brief would tell readers to always add a docs/decision-links.toml link. That is false and contradicts the plan's own D174.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-cli/src/backtest.rs:79-81 and decisions.rs only need a [[link]] for a 'superseded by', 'supersedes' or 'amends' hit, plus [[governs]] paths. Decision 4 says D174 avoids those phrases 'so no link is needed'. Step 2(c) still tells the reader to write 'record in a new appended decision, with a Provenance bullet and a docs/decision-links.toml link', and the criterion 1 test asserts that wording. Readers would then write criteria requiring a link with no matching hit. That is a criterion contradicting how Athena judges the log, the class this job fixes. Fix: Word rule (c) as follows: append a new decision with a Provenance bullet, never edit an existing entry. Add a docs/decision-links.toml [[link]] only when the new entry supersedes or amends an earlier one, or when the change touches a path listed under [[governs]]. Change the criterion 1 assertion to match.
findings.location: Plan Step 2 rule (c); Demonstration for criterion 1 item (c); Decision 4

findings.summary: The 'replace the phrase and check it is gone' assertion is a tautology. Whole-file substring pins can also be satisfied by test or comment copies.
findings.evidence: `source.replace(phrase, "x")` never contains the phrase, unless the phrase overlaps itself, so this assertion cannot fail and shows nothing about drift. The phrases also appear in test code: 'must cite commands that ran (D43)' at verify.rs:3341 and in athena-data records.rs:67, and 'docs/decisions.md is append-only' at mirrors.rs:1817. So a whole-file `contains` still passes if only the production message changes and a test or comment keeps the old text. Fix: Drop the tautological assertion. Anchor each pin to its production form, such as the `source: "..."` row in VERDICT_RULES or the format string at mirrors.rs:265. One way is to search only the text before `#[cfg(test)]`.
findings.location: Plan Step 4 and Demonstration for criterion 2 (third assertion)

findings.summary: The plan does not say which constant is pinned against checks.rs.
findings.evidence: Step 1 defines no constant whose wording comes from checks.rs. CHANGELOG_DEFAULT_PHRASE comes from admission.rs:999, and the rule that refuses a limiting criterion is DEFAULT_WRITTEN_FILES at checks.rs:574-577 ('Athena always adds it to a change reading...'). The table row for checks.rs has no defined phrase. Fix: Name the checks.rs pin explicitly. Either quote the DEFAULT_WRITTEN_FILES reason, or assert that every path in DEFAULT_WRITTEN_FILES appears in the section (see the first finding).
findings.location: Plan Step 4 and Demonstration for criterion 2 ('the changelog wording in reading/checks.rs')

findings.summary: Rule (d) repeats the existing Scope limit line in READING_RULES.
findings.evidence: READING_RULES[7] already says 'Scope limit: a limiting criterion lists CHANGELOG.md or says `the deliverables` ... (`check_scope_limit`)'. Fix: In rule (d), state only what is new: CHANGELOG.md is a default deliverable and a criterion must not forbid it. Point to the Scope limit rule for the rest instead of repeating it.

summary: The plan follows the request and the accepted reading. It adds information to the reader brief instead of a refusal rule, the files and functions it names exist (reader_brief at reader.rs:319, reference_and_rules_section at reader.rs:491, CHANGELOG_PATH at reading.rs:311), and every phrase it quotes is in the enforcing code as cited (verify.rs:601/1200/1227, mirrors.rs:265, athena-gate lib.rs:101, admission.rs:999). The CHANGELOG_PATH swap compiles through `use super::*` in checks.rs, and the reader_inputs fixture has a non-empty verifier_can_run, so the ordering assertion works. Two problems need a revision. First, the section and its pin test cover four hand-picked rules, not the class of rules that judge criteria. VERDICT_RULES in verify.rs also holds D63 (the whole-simple-command rule, which the plan itself relies on in decision 5), and a new verdict rule would leave the brief stale with no test failing. Criterion 2 asks for a test that fails when the enforcing rule changes and the brief does not, so this is the special case the request warns against. Second, the planned decision-log line tells readers to always add a docs/decision-links.toml link. The backtest needs a link only for a supersede or amend hit, and the plan's own D174 adds none, so the brief would state a false rule: the same class of failure this job is meant to fix. Smaller points: one drift assertion proves nothing, the pins match anywhere in a file, and it is unclear which constant pins checks.rs.
